evidence.text: The exact Commons file page identifies 前-seal.svg as a modern vector depiction of 前 in Shuowen seal-script style, says the picture is from the Sinica Database, and states that image is under CC0 1.0. The file history records the SVG as created with Inkscape in 2013 and updated in 2018. This is a modern redraw of a historical script form, not an artifact photograph. The page's search result was inspected, but direct page opens failed with a cache-miss error; its original image link is recorded as the candidate image URL.

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00355 前: Shuowen forms, graphic analysis and senses
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen's two distinct statements: cutting evenly, formed from 刀 with 歬 as phonetic; and forward motion, written 歬 (前), formed from 止 over 舟. It says the cutting graph was later used for directional 歬 and that a knife radical was added in popular writing to distinguish the cutting word, while recording 歬 as a variant of 前. It lists motion forward, spatial front, temporal earlier, future, historical predecessor and sequence/order senses. These are dictionary-recorded descriptions and citations, not a securely dated chronology of the senses.
evidence.title: A00355 前 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: character evolution; bronze and small-seal forms
evidence.text: The evolution page lists a bronze form indexed as 集成00068 and a Shuowen small-seal form. It describes 止 above 舟 as indicating a boat moving forward. This records one graphic interpretation, but does not establish the first lexical meaning or semantic chronology. Its footer states All Rights Reserved, so this evidence page is not treated as an image asset.
evidence.title: 漢字「前」：字形演變

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00355-003 歬: research note on graphic relationship and competing accounts
evidence.text: The entry calls 歬 a variant of 前 and quotes the Shuowen account of forward movement with 止 over 舟. It also records differing later explanations: Duan Yucai distinguishes the directional 歬 from a cutting graph, while another cited account treats a 刀-associated cutting graph as the source of the clerical form 前. The source preserves the conflict rather than deciding which graphic history came first.
evidence.title: [A00355-003] 歬 (前) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00364 剪: Shuowen analysis and reported graph use
evidence.text: The entry says Shuowen wrote the cutting graph as 前 and quotes 齊斷也。从刀，歬聲: ‘cut evenly,’ formed with 刀 and 歬 as phonetic. It gives later cutting uses, including a Tang poem citation, but those citations do not date the earliest use of the graph or establish a depicted tool's independent name and pronunciation.
evidence.title: A00364 剪 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The official Unihan page lists kMandarin qián and kHanyuPinyin qián, jiǎn. These are current character-reading metadata; they do not establish an ancient sound relationship or a sound-based borrowing history.

gaps: The Commons original SVG URL is established from the exact file description, but the web opener failed to fetch the SVG pixels. It is a modern seal-style redraw, not a photograph or direct reproduction of a dated inscription. The file's Commons description identifies the depicted graph and CC0 1.0 terms; the linked original Sinica data record was not independently opened here.

The official Unihan pages for 歬, 止, 舟, and 剪 could not be opened; local supplied rows are kept distinct from external evidence. No Baxter–Sagart row for 歬 or 剪 was supplied or verified, so no reconstructed reading comparison is claimed.

The record indexed as 集成00068 documents a bronze form, but no primary inscription passage was verified here that securely dates the earliest lexical attestation or establishes the order of motion, spatial-front, temporal-before, and cutting senses.

The competing traditional analyses leave unresolved whether the forward-direction word was first written 歬 and later with 前, or whether 前 began as a cutting graph later borrowed for the directional word. No independent original object name and pronunciation supports a depicted-tool borrowing claim; 前's reconstruction alone cannot prove that sound match.
No bulk source extract is recommended: no reuse terms for such an extract were verified, and character-specific records provide sufficient research value.
